description: Shared test cases of the transaction engine (backend Java and frontend TypeScript), PROMPT draft 6. Amounts are strings with 2 decimals. Defaults: account status ACTIVE, temporary false, creditLimit null; transaction fee 0.00, applied true, operationDate 2026-10-01T12:00:00, destination null. Each case expects either 'expected' (accounts and transactions to check, matched by id / uuid; transactions listed in application order; optional 'report' = income / expense / net of the applied transactions: ADDITION counts amount − fee, SUBTRACTION amount + fee, NEUTER only its fee as expense) or 'error' (first failing transaction; field/fieldCode only for VALIDATION_ERROR).

cases.name: INCOME credits amount minus fee; income = amount − fee
INCOME fee must be lower than the amount
INCOME cannot be pending
INCOME origin must be a SUPPLIER
A GROUP never participates in transactions
EXPENSE from STORAGE subtracts amount plus fee; expense = amount + fee
EXPENSE from STORAGE without enough funds
Pending EXPENSE from STORAGE does not touch the balance and does not count in reports yet
Pending EXPENSE is accepted without funds: they are validated when it is applied
EXPENSE from DEBTOR (credit card purchase) grows the debt; it is an expense the day of the purchase
EXPENSE from DEBTOR cannot exceed the credit limit
EXPENSE from a DEBTOR without credit line has no limit
Pending EXPENSE from DEBTOR does not grow the debt yet
EXPENSE destination must be a CONSUMER
TRANSFER moves A immediately and credits A minus fee; only the fee is an expense
Pending TRANSFER: money leaves the origin, the destination is credited when applied
TRANSFER without enough funds
TRANSFER requires a destination
Origin and destination must be different
INVEST from STORAGE to INVESTMENT
INVEST from INVESTMENT to BUSINESS
INVEST fee must be lower than the amount
PROFIT from BUSINESS to STORAGE with fee
Applied PROFIT from a temporary INVESTMENT disables it, even with remaining balance
A temporary account disabled by its PROFIT cannot be used later in the same batch
Pending PROFIT of a temporary account: the origin is debited but the account is disabled only when applied
DIVIDEND without destination credits the origin; income = amount − fee
DIVIDEND with destination credits the destination only
DIVIDEND cannot be pending
DIVIDEND fee must be lower than the amount
INTEREST on STORAGE is an expense
INTEREST on DEBTOR grows the debt and is an expense when it is charged
INTEREST on STORAGE without enough funds
INTEREST does not accept a fee
INTEREST does not accept a destination
BORROW lends money to a CREDITOR
BORROW without enough funds (no balance can become negative)
COLLECTION collects a loan
COLLECTION of more than what is owed is senseless
DEBT to STORAGE (cash loan) is not an expense; only its fee is
DEBT to STORAGE fee must be lower than the amount
DEBT to CONSUMER (purchase on credit) is an expense the day of the purchase
DEBT to CONSUMER does not accept a fee
DEBT cannot exceed the credit limit
PAYMENT reduces both balances and is not an expense (it settles a debt already recognized)
PAYMENT fee is paid by the STORAGE and is an expense; the debt goes down by the amount
PAYMENT of more than what is owed is senseless
PAYMENT needs funds for amount plus fee
PAYMENT cannot be pending
Disabled accounts cannot be used
Transactions are applied by operation date, not capture order
An expense dated before the income that funds it fails
Equal dates keep the capture order
Removing an intermediate income makes a later expense fail (recalculation from scratch)
Cents are exact: 0.10 + 0.20 = 0.30 and amounts round half up to 2 decimals
5.3 example: cash loan used and paid → expense 10,000, net −10,000
5.3 example: cash loan returned unused → nothing counts
5.3 example: credit card purchase and payment → expense 10,000 (on the purchase)
5.3 example: purchase on credit (DEBT → CONSUMER) and payment → expense 10,000
5.3 example: credit card interest and payment → expense 500
5.3 example: payment with fee → expense 50 (only the fee)
Full card cycle: purchase on credit, cash loan with fee, interest, then two payments
